properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): add_capability with id + allocated_to DID draw ALLOCATED_TO, and its reply said "This node already held exactly what this call passed; nothing moved". The revision note is computed from node PROPERTIES only, so every constructor that draws an edge in the same call asserts nothing moved when only the edge moved. Measured on add_capability, add_decision (related_to) and add_requirement (approver). The reporter's "probably not drawn" is OVERTURNED; the reply was false, not the write
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-25, reflow2 0.69.0 → 0.70.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "F-29 — `add_capability` with only `id` + `allocated_to` on an existing node answered "This node already held exactly what this call passed; nothing moved" — ambiguous about whether the ALLOCATED_TO edge was drawn. The follow-up `allocate` call then succeeded, so it probably had not been. The reply should say which edges it drew." EXPECTED: the reply says the ALLOCATED_TO edge was drawn, or says it was not. NOT AFFECTED: the create path of add_capability, where the node itself is new.

② PRECEDENT (searched on the reply's raw text): fact:root-cause-add-decision-discards-the-edge-echo-its-related-to-computed-2026-09-28 already measured that add_capability builds a `drawn` list (capture.rs ~1863) and discards it. That is the silence half of this report. chg:a-capability-carries-its-thread-in-one-call (2026-09-10, hxm F-02) built `allocated_to`. The "nothing moved" note has no record.

③ CANDIDATES:
(A) SILENT DROP. On a revise with unchanged properties, the handler returns before drawing the thread.
(B) FALSE REPLY. The edge is drawn and the note, computed over properties only, says nothing moved.
(C) DISCARDED ECHO. The edge is drawn and simply not named (the precedent).
(D) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. The later `allocate` "succeeding" proves nothing, because allocate on an existing edge also succeeds.
(E) OUTSIDE THE HANDLER. An older server on the reporter's side (0.69/0.70) behaved differently.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: read the edge set between the add_capability call and the allocate call. (A) predicts no edge. (B) and (C) predict the edge is present, and (B) also predicts the note says nothing moved. (D) predicts allocate's reply is identical whether or not the edge existed. (E) predicts a different shape in v0.70.0's source.

⑤ RESULTS (0.74.0 binary, scratch store; source at 70e547f):
· add_capability(cap:move-axis, name, description), then add_capability(id=cap:move-axis, allocated_to=cmp:motor). Reply keys: graph_id, loop_hint, node_id, node_type, properties, revision. revision = {added: [], replaced: [], changed: false, note: "This node already held exactly what this call passed; nothing moved."}. No edge named.
· Export immediately after: [cap:move-axis ALLOCATED_TO cmp:motor]. The edge WAS drawn. (A) REFUTED.
· allocate(cap:move-axis, cmp:motor) then replied {edge_type ALLOCATED_TO, from_id, to_id, properties {weight_basis: estimated}}, the same shape as a fresh draw, with no "already present", and the edge set was unchanged. (D) HOLDS: the reporter's follow-up could not distinguish the two cases, and it silently wrote weight_basis onto an edge that already existed.
· The same class on two other constructors: add_decision (existing exploratory, related_to only) and add_requirement (existing, approver only) each replied "nothing moved" while the export showed the new ANTICIPATES and AUTHORED_BY edges. (B) HOLDS at 3 of 3 constructors tested.
· Code: revision_of (capture.rs ~603) iterates `now.properties` against `prior.properties` only, and sets `changed = !replaced.is_empty() || !added.is_empty()`. It has no input for edges. It is called after the edges are drawn by add_capability (thread), add_decision (review_relations, sign_as_approver), add_requirement and add_design_rule (sign_as_approver). v0.70.0 has the identical shape (the discarded `drawn` list and the note text), so (E) is REFUTED.

⑥ CLASS: the reply describes a call from one of its two outputs. The revision block was built to guard PROPERTY loss (req:a-revising-write-says-what-it-removed), and its catch-all sentence "nothing moved" speaks for the whole call. Once constructors started drawing edges inline (satisfies/allocated_to 2026-09-10, approver 2026-09-06, related_to 2026-08-30), the sentence became false whenever only an edge moved. Same family as the 09-28 precedent ("each constructor hand-builds its reply, with no shared 'edges this call drew' block"). This finding adds that the silence is sometimes an assertion, not only an omission. A fix at the class (a call's reply is computed from the diff of node AND edge sets it made, through one shared helper) closes this, the precedent (add_decision/add_capability echo nothing) and the 09-23 related_to drop's invisibility at once. Rewording the note alone would not.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE (no code changed). A test pinning the class, over every constructor that can draw an edge (add_capability satisfies/allocated_to, add_decision related_to/approver, add_requirement and add_design_rule approver, add_verification verifies, add_change_event affected, record_finding caused_by): on an EXISTING node with unchanged properties, pass only the edge argument. Assert that the reply never says "nothing moved" when the edge set grew, and names each new edge. Also that allocate (and every edge helper) says whether the edge already existed. It fails today on at least 3 constructors plus allocate.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: "ambiguous about whether the ALLOCATED_TO edge was drawn" is HELD and understated: the reply asserts nothing moved. "it probably had not been" is OVERTURNED: it had been, and the confirming call (allocate) could not have told either way. "The reply should say which edges it drew" is HELD, and is the proposed fix, applied through one shared helper rather than per handler.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: add_design_rule was read, not run; it has the same sign_as_approver-then-revision_of shape. The reporter's store was not seen. The weight_basis overwrite by allocate on an existing edge was observed but not checked for loss (the fresh edge from add_capability carried no properties).
